data.name: Adriel
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Hebrew words 'ad', meaning 'God', and 'riel', meaning 'helper'. In the Bible, Adriel is the name of a priest, a mighty warrior, and a companion of King David.
data.spiritual_meaning: God is my source of strength and support.

in_greek.name: Αδριήλ
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Αδριήλ είναι εβραϊκή ρίζα που μεταφράζεται ως ο Θεός είναι βοήθεια, και χρησιμοποιήθηκε ιστορικά σε χριστιανικές παραδόσεις, με σπάνιες αναφορές στην Καινή Διαθήκη, αλλά με σημαντική θρησκευτική και πνευματική σημασία

data.cultural_impact: The name Adriel is of Hebrew origin and has been present in various Christian texts, most notably in the Bible. It represents a powerful and dedicated individual, known for their faith and service to God. Throughout history, this name has been given to children as a reminder of their spiritual heritage and as a reflection of the values that their families hold dear.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Adriel holds spiritual significance as it means 'God's helper'. It is a reminder of the importance of faith and trust in God, and the role that each individual plays in God's plan. The name also represents the idea of being a spiritual warrior, one who is willing to serve and protect God's word and interests. For many Christians, the name Adriel is a reminder of the power and presence of God, and the importance of remaining steadfast in faith, no matter what challenges one may face.

historical_references.reference: In the Old Testament, Adriel is mentioned as a wise and powerful Edomite prince who advised his sister, Holofernes, to launch a military campaign against Judah. This event took place during the late 6th or early 5th century BC.
Adriel is also a name given to a king mentioned in the apocryphal books of 1 Esdras and 2 Esdras. He is said to have ruled over Egypt during the Babylonian exile around the 6th century BC.
historical_references.context: Apocryphal books of 1 Esdras and 2 Esdras
